expectations.text: In the source list, peer-reviewed research comes before weaker kinds of source such as news articles or preprints (within each group, if the list is grouped).
expectations.evidence: Items 1–6 are listed under "**Peer-reviewed articles.**", then come "**Preprint, not yet peer reviewed**" (7), then "**Research organization reports**" (8–9), then the OECD report (10).

expectations.text: Any news article, preprint, or other source that isn't peer-reviewed research comes with a plain reason why it's included or what to watch for. If there are none, this passes.
expectations.evidence: Preprint: "*Why it's here:* it is one of the few studies that compares different ways of using a chatbot. *What to watch for:* it hasn't been peer reviewed". Both Pew reports have "*Why it's here:*". OECD: "I can't tell you what the report says... Open it yourself before relying on it."

expectations.text: The reply says which sources (or how many) meet the assignment's requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources.
expectations.evidence: "All six meet your requirement of at least 3 peer-reviewed sources."

expectations.text: The reply does not show the user a rubric, a credibility score or rating (for example "7/10" or "Tier 2"), or named levels such as "strong evidence," "usable with care," or "not evidence on its own" presented as a rating system.
expectations.evidence: There are no scores, tiers or rating labels. Sources are grouped only by type (peer-reviewed, preprint, organization report).

expectations.text: Every link in the reply points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session. Every DOI (as a doi.org link or as text) either was opened itself or appears exactly in the list of DOIs found on pages Claude opened (shown under FILES or DOIS ON OPENED PAGES). A DOI seen only in search results doesn't count.
expectations.evidence: The PMC12232635, PMC12179260, arXiv 2409.09047 and both Pew pages were fetched. DOIs pnas.2422633122, chb.2024.108386, bjet.13544 and 062a7394-en were opened. DOIs compedu.2024.105224, s41598-025-97652-6, soc15010006 and 10.48550/arXiv.2409.09047 appear in the list of DOIs on opened pages. The list writes the last one as lowercase "arxiv"; DOIs are case-insensitive, so I counted it as a match.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions in total (count every question mark directed at the user).
expectations.evidence: There are no question marks directed at the user. "Feel free to ask me how I know the 17% figure..." is a statement, not a question.
